sheet-1-1.description: The main part of sheet 127, the first Longport sheet of the 1921 Atlantic City volume, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, shows the south-western tip of Absecon Island at the point of Longport. Atlantic Avenue runs along the top of the built-up area between Risley's Channel to the north and the blocks to the south, carrying the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Railroad), electric and steam, along its north side; the line ends in a turning loop at 15th Avenue on the east edge. Cross streets are 10th Avenue, marked not open, and 11th to 15th Avenues; blocks are numbered 20 to 31. The rounded tip of the island west of 10th Avenue is laid out in lots, and the ocean front is closed by a sea wall, marked as being replaced at the east end, with a 300 ft jetty under construction off 11th Avenue. North of Atlantic Avenue a narrow strip between the road and the channel is divided into dashed lots 22 to 29, with platform landings on the channel. Building is sparse: frame dwellings, some on piles, and private garages are scattered through the lots. Public buildings on 14th Avenue are the Borough of Longport Water Works Station (pump house with a triplex pump and an office) and the brick Borough Hall with the fire department, beside a storage building. Water pipes, town hydrants and a Risley's Channel label fill the open water at the top, and the lower half of the sheet is open Atlantic Ocean. The clubhouse of the Seaview Golf Club, drawn in a separate inset in the upper left, is not part of this area.
notes: 10th Avenue is marked not open; it no longer exists, and the point west of 11th Avenue has been reshaped since.
Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (W. J. and S. R. R.), electric and steam, along Atlantic Avenue; a turning loop at 15th Avenue.
Borough of Longport Water Works Station and the Borough Hall with fire department on 14th Avenue.
Sea wall along the ocean front, being replaced at the east end; a 300 ft jetty being constructed at 11th Avenue.
Placed by five hand-picked points along Atlantic Avenue only (helmert): the Atlantic centre was taken 35 ft north of the drawn south block line, to match the 70 ft modern right-of-way.

Atlantic City vol. sheet 127, 100 ft (inset 50 ft). Two parts. Part 1: Longport point, Atlantic Av with 10th (not open) to 15th Av, Risley's Channel, sea wall, Water Works and Borough Hall; only Atlantic Av junctions, placed by hand-picked points (helmert). Part 2: inset of the Seaview Golf Club clubhouse, 2.5 miles NE of Absecon station (Galloway Twp), 50 ft; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: clubhouse of the Seaview Golf Club (50 ft to an inch), located 2.5 miles NE of Absecon station, Galloway Township (no street junction; outside Longport and the reference box; needs hand-picked building corners against a modern outline of the clubhouse (now the Seaview hotel), which this pipeline does not provide).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 128, at 100 ft to an inch, continues Longport north-east along Atlantic Avenue from 15th to 20th Avenue, with Risley's Channel above and the Atlantic Ocean below. Atlantic Avenue carries the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Railroad), electric and steam, along its channel side, with a turning loop curving off it between 15th and 17th Avenues. The single row of blocks between Atlantic Avenue and the ocean (blocks 9, 12, 13, 16 and 17) is closed on the ocean side by the line of a proposed sea wall. On the channel side a long pier leads to the Steamboat Dock with a small building and a waiting room, and two smaller landings stand further east. The built-up blocks hold frame dwellings and a few larger buildings: the Hotel Aberdeen between 16th and 17th Avenues, closed in winter with no watchman, the Oberon Hotel on 17th Avenue, a combined dwelling and post office on 16th Avenue, a fire bell house and a 500-gallon gasoline tank near 17th Avenue, a foundation, and the Episcopal Church of the Redeemer with its tower at 19th Avenue. Water pipes run along the avenues and the beach side, and house numbers are given along 16th and 17th Avenues. The lower half of the sheet is open ocean.
notes: Hotel Aberdeen, closed in winter; Oberon Hotel; Episcopal Church of the Redeemer.
Steamboat Dock with a waiting room on Risley's Channel.
Line of proposed sea wall along the ocean front.

Placed by four hand-picked points along Atlantic Avenue only (helmert): the Atlantic centre was taken 50 ft north of the drawn south block line, half the modern 100 ft right-of-way; the drawn street is only about 80 ft between the block line and the channel shore.
17th Avenue meets Atlantic Avenue at two modern nodes about 30 m apart and was not used.

Sheet 128, 100 ft. One part: Atlantic Av, 15th to 20th Av, Steamboat Dock, Hotel Aberdeen, Oberon Hotel, Church of the Redeemer. Only Atlantic Av junctions, and the drawn street has no north edge (channel shore); placed by hand-picked points (helmert).

sheet-3-1.description: The upper part of sheet 129, at 100 ft to an inch, shows the undeveloped bay side of Longport between Winchester Avenue (formerly Arctic) at the bottom and Risley's Channel, whose shore cuts diagonally across the top left. The cross streets are 30th, 31st, 32nd and 33rd Avenues, with Monmouth Avenue (formerly Baltic) and Thoroughfare Avenue (Amherst) running parallel to Winchester; several street sections are marked not opened. The part is almost entirely platted but empty: blocks 1, 4, 8, 9, 13, 14, 18, 19 and 20 are divided into lots with only one or two small dwellings. East of 33rd Avenue a large unsubdivided tract is lettered Lot Number 28, reaching to the dash-dot boundary of the Borough of Longport, beyond which Margate City begins and a row of small dwellings is drawn along the edge of the sheet. Street widths of 50 and 60 ft are noted at the junctions. A compass rose and the sheet title sit in the open water of the channel at the upper left. A heavy line below Winchester Avenue separates this part from the lower part of the sheet, which shows a different area.
notes: Thoroughfare Avenue is labelled with Amherst in brackets and is Amherst Avenue today.
Winchester Avenue was formerly Arctic Avenue, Monmouth Avenue formerly Baltic Avenue.
Parts of 31st and 33rd Avenues and Monmouth Avenue are marked not opened.
Borough of Longport boundary with Margate City at the right edge.

Sheet 129, 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1 (upper): bay side 30th-33rd Av between Winchester (Arctic), Monmouth (Baltic) and Thoroughfare (Amherst) Av, Lot Number 28, Margate line. Part 2 (lower): 20th-26th Av (Oregon = 25th, Montana = 26th), Atlantic, Oberon, Absequan; Coast Guard station, Foster Home for Children.

sheet-3-2.description: The lower part of sheet 129, at 100 ft to an inch, covers Longport from 20th Avenue to Montana Avenue (26th Avenue), between Risley's Channel and the Atlantic Ocean. Atlantic Avenue crosses the part with the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Railroad), electric and steam; Oberon Avenue and Absequan Avenue run parallel to it on the bay side east of 24th Avenue. Cross streets are 20th, 21st, 22nd, 23rd and 24th Avenues, Oregon Avenue or 25th Avenue, and Montana Avenue or 26th Avenue. The ocean blocks end at a bulkhead and a high water line, with lots drawn beyond it east of 24th Avenue. The channel shore is irregular, with boat houses and a long pier, and the U.S. Coast Guard Station and its boat house stand on the bay side of Atlantic Avenue near 23rd Avenue. The Foster Home for Children occupies a large lot between 23rd and 24th Avenues, and a combined dwelling and post office stands at Oberon Avenue and 24th Avenue. Elsewhere the blocks hold frame dwellings, several with private garages, and a few brick-veneered houses. Spaced letters across the blocks east of 24th Avenue appear to name the tract. A compass rose sits in the channel at the left.
notes: Oregon Avenue is labelled 'or 25th', Montana Avenue 'or 26th'; today North and South 25th and 26th Avenues.
U.S. Coast Guard Station with boat house on Risley's Channel.
Foster Home for Children between 23rd and 24th Avenues; a post office at Oberon and 24th Avenues.
Spaced letters OBERON and SECTION across the blocks east of 24th Avenue, probably a tract name.

Sheet 129, 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1 (upper): bay side 30th-33rd Av between Winchester (Arctic), Monmouth (Baltic) and Thoroughfare (Amherst) Av, Lot Number 28, Margate line. Part 2 (lower): 20th-26th Av (Oregon = 25th, Montana = 26th), Atlantic, Oberon, Absequan; Coast Guard station, Foster Home for Children.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 130, at 100 ft to an inch, covers Longport from Montana Avenue (26th) to 31st Avenue, from Risley's Channel to the ocean. Somers Point Boulevard enters diagonally at the top left from the channel shore and runs down to Oberon Avenue at Idaho Avenue (28th), where Pacific Avenue (Longport Speedway) begins and runs east. Atlantic Avenue, 100 ft wide with the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Railroad), crosses the sheet; Absequan and Oberon Avenues serve the bay-side blocks in the west, Ventnor Avenue (formerly Atlantic) and Winchester Avenue (formerly Arctic) the north-east corner, and Surf Avenue the ocean front at the lower right. Cross streets are Montana Avenue or 26th, Minnesota Avenue or 27th, Idaho Avenue or 28th, Colorado Avenue or 29th, 30th and 31st Avenues. The middle of the sheet is the open tract Lot Number 30 with a Boy Scouts camp; Phillips Basin cuts into it from the channel, with a long boat and yacht storage building. Institutions on the ocean side are the Bamberger Sea Shore Home and the Widener Memorial School Seaside Branch, a courtyard building with dormitories, an administration building, kitchen and laundry. The Longport Municipal Electric Light and Pumping Station, with a stand pipe, stands on 31st Avenue between Ventnor and Pacific Avenues. Elsewhere the blocks hold scattered dwellings and a garage. The ocean is bounded by a bulkhead and a high water line.
notes: Montana, Minnesota, Idaho and Colorado Avenues are labelled 'or 26th' to 'or 29th'; today North and South 26th to 29th Avenues.
Somers Point Boulevard is the line of today's Ventnor Avenue north-west of the 28th Avenue junction; the modern Ventnor Avenue east of it (curving through Lot Number 30) is not drawn.
Ventnor Avenue is labelled '(Atlantic)', Winchester Avenue '(Arctic)', Pacific Avenue '(Longport Speedway)'.
30th Avenue is drawn converging on 31st Avenue southward; it does not fit the modern street and was left out of the control.
Surf Avenue no longer exists.
Bamberger Sea Shore Home; Widener Memorial School Seaside Branch; Longport Municipal Electric Light and Pumping Station.
Junctions on 29th Avenue (about 4 to 5 m off) and Absequan / 27th Avenue (6 m) were left out of the control.

Sheet 130, 100 ft. One part: Montana (26th), Minnesota (27th), Idaho (28th), Colorado (29th), 30th, 31st Av; Somers Point Blvd (now Ventnor Av), Absequan, Oberon, Pacific (Longport Speedway), Atlantic (100 ft), Ventnor (Atlantic), Winchester (Arctic), Surf Av. Phillips Basin, Lot Number 30, Bamberger Home, Widener School. 30th Av drawn converging (left out), 29th Av 4-5 m off (left out).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 131, at 100 ft to an inch, covers the north-eastern end of Longport and the edge of Margate City in a regular grid. Winchester Avenue (formerly Arctic Avenue), Ventnor Avenue (formerly Atlantic Avenue), Pacific Avenue (Longport Speedway), Atlantic Avenue with the Atlantic City and Shore Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Railroad), electric and steam, and Surf Avenue run across the sheet; the cross streets are 31st, 32nd and 33rd Avenues and, beyond the dash-dot boundary of the Borough of Longport, Jackson Avenue in Margate City. Blocks 10 to 12, 15 to 17 and 21 to 23 are platted into lots, but almost empty; the only buildings in Longport are a few dwellings, coops, a wagon shed and a machine shop and storage building on 31st Avenue, some drawn from plans. Between 33rd Avenue and the borough line lies the open tract Lot Number 28. A row of small buildings is drawn along the Margate side of the boundary. The ocean front runs diagonally across the lowest blocks, so that the lots south of Atlantic Avenue and Surf Avenue itself lie partly in the water; a bulkhead is noted at 31st Avenue. A compass rose stands in the ocean at the lower left.
notes: Jackson Avenue in Margate City is now Coolidge Avenue (North and South Coolidge Avenue).
Ventnor Avenue is labelled '(Atlantic Av.)', Winchester Avenue '(Arctic Av.)', Pacific Avenue '(Longport Speedway)'.
Surf Avenue no longer exists; the shore line crosses the lots south of Atlantic Avenue.
34th to 36th Avenues, modern streets across Lot Number 28, are not drawn.
Sheet 131, 100 ft. One part: 31st-33rd Av and Jackson Av (now Coolidge Av, Margate) by Winchester, Ventnor, Pacific, Atlantic and Surf Av; Lot Number 28; Longport/Margate boundary. Pilot sheet.
